title: stateful-service-cache-drain-rolling-deploy-playbook-2026
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary:
This runbook defines a safe, repeatable process for performing rolling deployments of stateful platform services that hold in-memory or sharded KV prefix caches (examples: kv-prefix-cache, runtime-router, model-kv-shard). The goal is to update code or configuration with minimal impact to latency SLOs and to avoid mass cache eviction that would spike downstream token cost and tail latency.

Intended audience:
- Platform operators
- Release engineers
- Oncall SREs

Key risks addressed:
- Cold-cache storms causing 99th percentile token latency spikes
- Traffic blackholing during leader handoff for sharded services
- Uncoordinated restarts triggering cascading evictions

When to use this runbook:
1. Rolling restarts for stateful services with in-memory caches or KV shards.
2. Configuration changes that affect cache schema, shard assignment, or in-process warmup behavior (e.g., cache-ttl, prefetch hints, shard-count).
3. Emergency patching where fast but safe rollout is required.

Preflight checklist (operator must verify before starting):
1) Ownership and windows:
   - Confirm owner: platform-service-team (pager: #platform-ops).
   - Approved maintenance window: low-traffic period for affected region(s).
2) Monitoring and SLOs:
   - Baseline 1m and 5m error budget burn for service < 1%.
   - Baseline 99th latency for token-serving endpoints (api/v1/generate) and cache-miss latency.
3) Capacity and fallback:
   - Ensure at least 2x spare capacity in same-region routing pool.
   - Verify fallback model variants are available and routable.
4) Artifact verification:
   - Container image built and scanned. Tag format: service-name@sha256:...
   - Feature gate flags evaluated in staging.
5) Runbook and rollback prepared:
   - Confirm rollback image and tested A/B in staging.
   - Reserved operator for manual rollback.

Preflight operator commands (examples):
- Verify leader health and shard distribution:
  curl -sS https://runtime-proxy.internal/_shard_status | jq .
- Check cache hit ratio (PromQL):
  sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total[5m]))
- Confirm available replicas and pod readiness:
  kubectl get sts/kv-prefix-cache -n platform -o wide

Rollout strategy overview:
We use a staggered, warm-drain -> restart -> validate pattern per pod to avoid bulk cache loss. For highly sharded services we coordinate shard reassignment with a 2-phase drain: soft-drain (stop accepting new writes, continue serving reads) then hard-drain (evict local routing tokens) before pod termination.

Parameters (defaults, can be tuned per-service):
- batch_size: 1 pod at a time per zone
- soft_drain_timeout: 60s
- hard_drain_timeout: 90s
- validation_window: 5 minutes
- allowed_slo_perturbation: +15% 99p latency

Detailed step-by-step procedure:
1) Initiate maintenance ticket and pin routing rule:
   - Create ticket in tracker and post on #platform-ops channel.
   - Activate temporary routing tag: route:prefer-warm-backends=false (prevents cold prefills from new traffic).

2) Start first pod sequence (repeat for each pod in batch):
   a) Soft drain: mark pod as not accepting new cache-affecting writes.
      - API: POST /admin/pods/{pod}/actions with body {"action":"soft_drain"}
      - Wait up to soft_drain_timeout for connections to drop to < 10 active.
   b) Validate soft drain: ensure read hit ratio stays stable and requests are served.
      - PromQL check (expect <5% increase in miss rate):
        increase(kv_cache_misses_total[5m]) / increase(kv_cache_requests_total[5m]) < 0.05
   c) Hard drain: trigger shard handoff and persist any in-memory deltas to durable store.
      - API: POST /admin/pods/{pod}/actions {"action":"handoff_and_flush"}
      - Confirm /_handoff_status returns {"state":"complete"}.
   d) Pod restart: kubectl rollout restart statefulset/kv-prefix-cache -n platform --field-selector metadata.name={pod}
   e) Post-restart warmup: wait for pod readiness + warmup hooks (pod readiness not sufficient)
      - Call readiness-warmup endpoint: POST /internal/warmup?strategy=prefetch&limit=200
      - Monitor warming progress via metric: kv_prefetch_items_total (expect > 100 items within 3 minutes)
   f) Validation window: observe 5-minute window for regression signals:
      - 99th latency increase <= allowed_slo_perturbation
      - Error rate change <= 0.5% absolute
      - Token cost per 5m bucket not spiking > 20% baseline
   g) If validations pass, proceed to next pod. If not, trigger rollback for this batch (see rollback steps).

3) Canary parallelism rules:
   - If cluster spans multiple AZs, perform one pod per AZ simultaneously to retain cross-AZ redundancy.
   - If a single AZ handles > 60% of traffic, reduce batch_size to 1 globally.

Rollback (immediate actions):
- If 99th latency > baseline + 25% or error rate > baseline + 2% for validation_window, perform emergency rollback:
  1) Revert routing tag to previous state to send traffic away from warmed pods.
  2) kubectl set image statefulset/kv-prefix-cache kv-prefix-cache=service-name@<rollback-sha> -n platform
  3) Mark rollout paused and open incident with priority P1.
  4) Rehydrate cache by invoking emergency-prefill (see emergency-prefill below) once rollback completes.

Emergency-prefill (recovering from mass cold cache):
- When global miss rate is high and token costs spike, run a prioritized prefetch using historical hotspots. Steps:
  1) Generate hotkey list from recent telemetry: top 1k prefixes by weight.
  2) Call internal batch prefetch API: POST /internal/prefetch with body {"keys":[...], "priority":"emergency"}
  3) Throttle prefill to keep added traffic under 10% of normal baseline to avoid cascading load.

Observability and dashboards to watch (links):
- Cache Health Dashboard: /d/cache-health (panels: hit ratio, misses by prefix, prefetch throughput)
- Rolling Deploy Monitor: /d/rollouts (panels: per-pod warmup status, handoff latencies)
- Cost Explorer: /d/token-cost (panels: per-tenant token spend, 5m delta)
- Alerting rules to consider:
  - Alert: KVCacheMissSpree (firing when miss_rate > 0.4 for 10m) -> Severity: P3
  - Alert: 99pTokenLatencySpike (99p > baseline * 1.25 for 5m) -> Severity: P2

Prometheus / PromQL snippets:
- Pod warmup completion: increase(kv_prefetch_items_total[5m]) > 50
- Hotkey thrash: topk(20, sum by(prefix)(increase(kv_cache_requests_total[5m])))

Post-deploy validation (24h checklist):
1) Daily drift: Ensure overall hit ratio back within 2% of baseline.
2) Error budget burn remains < 2% for the next 24h.
3) Compare token-per-request cost between pre and post - investigate >10% delta.
4) Run a regression eval using the standard prompt-set against routed model variants to detect quality regressions (link: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks).

Known failure modes and mitigations:
- Slow shard handoff: extend hard_drain_timeout to 180s and reduce batch_size.
- Pod fails readiness after restart: automatically mark pod for manual triage and roll back that instance only.
- Persistent drop in hit ratio: schedule a targeted re-prefetch and analyze eviction patterns.

Operational notes and ownership matrix:
- Primary operator: platform-service-team (pager #platform-ops)
- Escalation: eng-sre (pager #eng-sre) after 30 minutes unresolved
- Product impact owner: runtime-product (email runtime-product@redwood.ai)

Appendix: example CLI snippets
- Warm drain via admin API:
  curl -X POST "https://runtime-proxy.internal/admin/pods/pod-12/actions" -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN" -d '{"action":"soft_drain"}'
- Trigger rolling restart for a single pod (statefulset):
  kubectl patch pod pod-12 -n platform -p '{"metadata":{"annotations":{"rollout-timestamp":"$(date -u +%s)"}}}'
